📂 MASTER FIELD MANUAL: PASSIVE RECONNAISSANCE (OSINT)

Tags: #Reconnaissance #OSINT #PassiveRecon #DNS #WHOIS #RDAP #Shodan
code Code

[Phase 1: Domain & Identity] ──> [Phase 2: DNS & Subdomains] ──> [Phase 3: Global Infrastructure]
      (WHOIS / RDAP)                 (dig / crt.sh / Dumpster)               (Shodan / Censys)

```
==**1. Core Rule: Active vs. Passive**==
```

>     ==**Active Reconnaissance:**==
>      Packets hit the target directly (==nmap==, ==ping==). Leaves IP entries in firewalls, WAFs, and SIEM logs.

>     ==**Passive Reconnaissance:**== 
>     Queries third-party aggregators and public databases. Zero direct packets sent to the target. Completely invisible to the target's SOC.

> **==2. Domain & Ownership Intel (WHOIS vs. RDAP)==**

    WHOIS (==TCP Port 43==): Plaintext ASCII query protocol. Output varies by registrar.

>         ==**Query:**== 
```
>         ==whois target.com==
```
> 
>         ==**Filtered:**== 
```
>         ==whois target.com | grep -iE "Registrar:|Name Server:|Creation Date|Expiration Date"==
```
> 
>     RDAP (==HTTPS Port 443==): Modern standard. RESTful, encrypted, machine-readable JSON.
> 
>         ==**Query with jq:**==
```
>          ==curl -s https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/target.com | jq .==
```
> 
>         ==**Extract Nameservers:**==
```
>          ==curl -s https://rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/target.com | jq '.nameservers'==
```

3. **==DNS Interrogation (dig on UDP/TCP Port 53)**==

>     ==**Stealth Query via Public Resolver:**==
```
    ==dig @1.1.1.1 target.com [RECORD_TYPE]==
```

>     ==**(Queries Cloudflare instead of target's nameserver; preserves zero footprint).**==

>     ==**Script-Friendly Output:**==
```
    ==dig +short target.com [RECORD_TYPE]==
```

    Record Types & Exploitation Angles:

>         ==**==A== (IPv4) / ==AAAA== (IPv6): Compare both. IPv6 addresses frequently lack the WAF/firewall rules applied to IPv4.**==
> 
>         ==**CNAME (Canonical Name / Alias): Points a subdomain to an external service (e.g., GitHub, S3 bucket). If the external service is deleted but the CNAME remains, execute a ==**Subdomain Takeover.==**
> 
>         **==MX (Mail Exchange): Lower priority number = primary server. Secondary/backup mail servers (e.g., priority 10 or 20) are often unpatched.==**
> 
>         **==TXT: Contains email anti-spoofing policies (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) and verification tokens. If DMARC is p=none or SPF is loose (~all), email spoofing/phishing is viable.==**
> 
>     **==TTL (Time To Live): Indicates DNS cache duration in seconds. Unusually low TTLs (e.g., 60s) signal live infrastructure migration.**==

> ==**4. Subdomain Discovery (Certificate Transparency & Aggregation)**==

>     ==**Certificate Transparency (==crt.sh==):**==

        Public, append-only cryptographic ledger of all SSL/TLS certificates issued by CAs.1

>         ==**Web Query:**==
```
         ==https://crt.sh/?q=%.target.com== (Wildcard search).
```

>         ==**CLI Query (JSON):**== 
```
        ==curl -s "https://crt.sh/?q=%.target.com&output=json" | jq -r '.[].name_value' | sort -u==
```

        Value: Exposes hidden staging (dev.), internal portals (admin.), and legacy servers that requested HTTPS certificates.

>     ==**DNSDumpster (dnsdumpster.com):**==

        Scrapes search engine caches and historical DNS datasets.

        Maps relational graphs (Root Domain -> MX -> Nameservers -> Subdomains -> ASNs/Hosting Providers).

> 5. **==Internet-Wide Asset Discovery (Shodan / Censys)**==

    Mechanism: Indexes the IPv4 space 24/7 via automated port scanning and Banner Grabbing (capturing service response headers).

>     ==**Key Search Operators:==**
> 
>         **==hostname:"target.com" (Finds servers linked to domain).==**
> 
>         **==org:"Target Corporation" (Filters by registered enterprise IP space).==**
> 
>         **==product:"Apache" port:80 (Finds specific technologies).==**
> 
>         **==country:"US" (Geographic filtering).**==

    Critical Findings:

        Recursion: enabled on DNS (Port 53): Vulnerable to cache poisoning and amplification DDoS.

        Exposed databases (Port 3306 MySQL, Port 6379 Redis, Port 27017 MongoDB) with default/empty credentials.
